chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Abbas ibn Aamir, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from his father, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When you are certain that you have had an occurrence (of breaking ablution), so perform ablution, and beware of renewing an ablution ever, until you are certain that you have had an occurrence.'

key_terms.أَحْدَثْتَ: You have had an occurrence (of breaking ritual purity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing wudu when in doubt about whether an event occurred?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi articulates the principle of *al-istishab* (presumption of continuity) in Shia jurisprudence, asserting that the original state of purity remains valid until certainty of its breaking occurs. It distinguishes between mere doubt (*shakk*) and certainty (*yaqin*), preventing unnecessary ritual burden (*ghil*) on the worshipper. This ruling is foundational for understanding how minor impurities are handled in daily prayers, emphasizing that doubt alone does not invalidate the previous act of worship.
